So, there's a new Lord of the Rings game, and in the opening sequence the main character and Celebrimbor build their own Ring of Power. I'm not a hardcore Tolkienist, but isnt' this a really bad idea lorewise?
Building a New Ring of Power in Lord of the Rings

I'm not an expert on the lore either, but I find this curious. Can you provide more context about the second ring? The ring of power represented dominance and subjugation. It wasn't a tool to grant Sauron more power or elevate him to a higher state. It simply oppressed everyone else. The ring was subject to Sauron, and the lesser rings were subject to the one ring. It created a hierarchy where Sauron placed himself at the top. Even having possession of the one ring didn't put you on the same level as Sauron. As established in the books, trying to use the ring against Sauron would be futile because the ring would betray the wearer.

Creating a second ring of power would not grant the wearer an advantage over Sauron. It would only make a second player in the oppression game. That's why I'm curious about the context of this second ring. Are they trying to use it to defeat Sauron? If the writers understand the themes in LotR, it won't end well. It would be like a third world corrupt dictatorship being overthrown by a corrupt rebellion. Just a constant cycle of corruption, or, in the case of middle earth, oppression.
I think Celebrimbor, in the dlc of the first game, had an ambition of ruling Mordor and the Orcs. That's why they forged the new One Ring, to take control of what Sauron has.

Basically, at the end of the game, Talion persuades Celebrimbor not to depart for Valinor but instead oppose Sauron, convincing him that he couldn't be at peace in Valinor knowing what Sauron was doing back in Middle Earth. It's at this point that Celebrimbor muses that perhaps it is time for a new Ring of Power.

As for whether Sauron's Ring would overcome a new Ring of Power forged by Celebrimbor itself: difficult to say. First, Celebrimbor did forge the Three: those rings Sauron did not know about until they were already forged and done, and he had no power over them. Even so, the elves had to take great care to hide the Three for fear that eventually Sauron would find them and either capture them or bend them to his will. The Seven and the Nine were all forged by Celebrimbor with Sauron taking a hand in the process, and so were irretrievably tainted.

A new Ring of Power forged in secret by Celebrimbor might have the same qualities as the Three did: if Sauron had no hand in their creation, he could not have influence over that Ring either unless it was captured and brought to him. I think Celebrimbor's new Ring of Power would have to be inferior to that which Sauron created: the One Ring is not just a ring, Sauron poured much of himself into it, making it a very potent force of magic at least. Whatever Ring of Power Celebrimbor plans on making, it's probably going to be a ring of war: something that turns Talion into a more powerful commander of forces.
